_comment: Citations retrieved and verified AT DRAFT TIME via the Firecrawl research tools, 2026-09-21. Each was resolved by inspect_paper and the title stored EXACTLY as returned — not reformatted, not from memory. A citation carried over from a previous round has not been verified at this draft time and does not count.

citations.title: Efficacy of dietary supplements containing isolated organic compounds for weight loss: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised placebo-controlled trials.
citations.source_note: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 67 randomised placebo-controlled trials. Preferred over any single trial; no society guideline on OTC weight-loss drops specifically was found.

citations.title: Continued Risk of Dietary Supplements Adulterated With Approved and Unapproved Drugs: Assessment of the US Food and Drug Administration's Tainted Supplements Database 2007 Through 2021.
citations.source_note: Assessment of the FDA's own Tainted Dietary Supplement Database — a regulator's surveillance record rather than an investigator's trial.

citations.title: Biotin for the treatment of nail disease: what is the evidence?
citations.source_note: Review of the biotin/nail literature. NOTE: findings run AGAINST the drafter's prior — small trials do show improvement in brittle nails. Recorded as the literature says it, not as assumed.

citations.title: Vitamins and minerals: their role in nail health and disease.
citations.source_note: PMID only; no DOI returned. The gate accepts a resolved PMID or DOI, and this resolves.

citations.title: Strategies for mitigating risk posed by biotin interference on clinical immunoassays.
citations.source_note: The emergency-medicine-specific point: high-dose biotin interferes with streptavidin-based immunoassays, troponin among them. Squarely within his own specialty rather than borrowed from dermatology.
